 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. After Jared McCain's strong Sixth Man start to the season, his play has dipped badly. Now the Oklahoma City Thunder need him to step up if they're going to stay afloat in the Wild West. Consistency has been a confusing issue for him so far, and they need more from him this time.
 McCain comes off as a promising talent that the Thunder snagged off the Philadelphia 76ers at last season's trade deadline. So far, it does seem that he's a huge spark off the bench. But with Oklahoma City's current predicament, McCain needs to take it up a notch.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement McCain's Shooting Has Been a Nightmare for OKC
 Nov 10, 2026; Portland, Oregon, USA; Oklahoma City Thunder guard Jared McCain (3) spots up to shoot the ball against Portland Trail Blazers guard Damian Lillard (0) during the first half at Moda Center. Mandatory Credit: Jaime Valdez-Imagn Images
 After McCain's blazing postseason run with OKC last season, the guard is now just shooting a career-low 32.8% from three this year. That's a huge drop from his first two seasons, where he logged over 38% between Philly and OKC. That's just one of the Thunder's shooting issues that need to be addressed this season.
 As a guard coming off the bench with Ajay Mitchell now starting , McCain wouldn't be the first to have some difficulty finding a consistent rhythm. However, it does seem that he's slowly finding his way as he gets to his spots and becomes more comfortable.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Considering OKC's lack of notable sharpshooters after their surprising offseason trades, McCain has a huge role to step into. He's already shown that he's not afraid of the big moments in the NBA Playoffs, so expect to see more improvements from his shooting moving forward.
 Playmaking Needs Huge Improvement from McCain
 It's no secret that OKC is missing the reliable second-option scoring and playmaking from the injured Jalen Williams . With Mitchell moving up to the starter role, McCain takes the sixth man spot in his place. That's when he's expected to run the second unit and create plays for his teammates.
 The problem is, McCain is a notable sharpshooter but isn't quite praised for his playmaking. In fact, his assists regressed after arriving in OKC, dropping to a career-low of 0.9 dimes per game. This year, he's generating at least 1.8 assists per game.
 That's not too bad a number for a guard who's expected to prioritise his own shot whenever he has the ball. Mitchell was supposed to be the floor general for the second unit, and now McCain has to step up on this part of his game if OKC is going to find ways to keep him on the court without sacrificing ball movement.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Still a Better Season from McCain
 Regardless of his struggles, statistically, McCain is mostly improving on his first OKC season. He's averaging his best numbers in a Thunder uniform, even with what is presumably a cold stretch from three. Crucially, he's been rampaging his way to the rim with better paint scoring (67.7% from within five feet) — reminiscent of his early days in Philly.
 Like Mitchell, he's engaged in a bigger role than ever, and he's starting to show flashes of what he can do when the team trusts him to deliver. It may be a hit-or-miss with his rhythm, but OKC is definitely confident enough to let him chuck up the shots he needs to catch fire and deliver for the team.
 If you're going to take a look at McCain's post-trade 2025-26 with the Thunder , it's fair to say that he's definitely more comfortable than ever. McCain is running better plays with the team. The three-pointer may not fall for him all the time, but he's shown that he's lethal when he knocks them down. That's something to hope for in more important games.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Last Word
 OKC fans may have forgotten the fact that McCain is only 22. He's a year older than fast-developing rookie Aday Mara . That just means that he's got a lot of room for improvement. The Thunder guard is learning from watching Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's heroics next to him, and he's on a team that's still yearning for a dynasty.
 McCain is in the right place at this point in his career. That means he's got all the time in the world to improve and prove his mettle by helping to carry the load for this injured OKC team.
